units.title: Carrow Point readings, day 8.
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 07:00: 1022.8 hPa and falling slowly, air 8.4 C, dew point 8.1 C, visibility 150 m. Wind southwest 1, the first breath of it in five days. Fog signal still sounding. Prediction: the breeze builds this afternoon and the fog breaks from the west after dark. Advection fog week, final instalment, I hope.

units.title: Rope Walk recycling: collected.
units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Victory, of a kind. Rope Walk recycling was collected at 07:40 this morning. The crew said the lorry 'went into the fog and came out with a dent'. I quoted the newsletter's 'normal day next week' back at the driver and he said 'if you say so', which I have written down. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.title: Fog delays, day 8.
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Day 8 report: 20 minutes late, horn every two minutes, nobody with a stopwatch. Progress. The Lisle buoy is still dark and three separate passengers informed the crew of it. The mate's face suggested this was not news to her, or to anyone on the Sound.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: As promised, side by side with the register entry. 1. The real description is 'Total vegetation clearance, Kittering Holm' and nothing more. 2. In the screenshot the added words are in a slightly narrower typeface and sit a pixel low. 3. The reference number in the screenshot is not the Holm's. It belongs to a garage extension in Tollinby, determined last month. Someone pasted a sentence into the wrong picture.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What would we expect to see if the Holm really were a designated evacuation site? A civil contingencies plan, a consultation, council minutes, a budget line, signage, a road. We see none of it: only a clearance consent and a screenshot with the wrong reference number. The simplest explanation is someone's joke that got away from them.

units.title: Slipway figure: questions worth asking.
units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Reading Harbour Chat. Before anyone builds a legend, what would we expect if it were a person? Prints in the weed on the slip, a car on the quay, someone seen walking up through the village afterwards. Has anyone asked the chip shop? Fog shortens apparent distance and lengthens apparent height: a figure at forty metres in fog reads taller than it is.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Well done, Bernard. At Dellow the bins on 3 still haven't been touched and the management office calls it a 'contractor matter'. Everything is a contractor matter. I am going to become a contractor so I can complain to myself and be ignored more efficiently.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: To Ewan's question: the custom is recorded in Gilliver since at least the 1880s, and I have written it up on the Society wiki this morning, with sources. Briefly, those who keep it call it a courtesy, and the 'they' changes with the person you ask. Maud very kindly gave the Society an interview some years ago, which is in the holdings.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Then who made it? I never said it was real, I said someone sent it to me. If I'm being blamed for asking, that tells you something as well. Here it is again for anyone who missed it, before it gets buried by people who would rather not look. Save a copy.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Moderator note. I have removed the screenshot from the opening post and the repost above. The council has confirmed the image is altered, and the reference number on it belongs to another application. Gil, nobody is blaming you for asking, but I will not leave a doctored document on this board. Thread locked. General Holm discussion can continue in 'What is the Holm actually for?'. Pell, admin.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: If I may. A data centre needs a great deal of electricity and a great deal of cooling water, and the Holm has neither a cable nor a spring worth the name. I taught the water cycle to Lisle children for thirty-four years, and I would have marked 'data centre on the Holm' with a gentle question mark. Mrs Hale (retd.)

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Ewan, since you invoke me: 'Who are they, though?' is perfectly good English in conversation. 'You lot' I will let pass, this once. The lamps were a favourite subject for my class projects, and every single child came back with a different answer from their grandmother, which taught them more about history than any textbook.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: On the data centre: no grid connection application, no subsea cable notice from the Coastguard, no water abstraction licence, and all three would be public. On the retreat: no harbour works consent. On the refuge: what would a refuge need that a cleared island gives and a wooded one doesn't? I can't think of anything. My guess remains land speculation.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: it was a lad on the slip. it's always a lad on the slip. somebody's nephew in his dad's coat. case closed, next.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Sightlines, Ferrous. A cleared island means you can see anyone coming from every side. Think about who needs that. I'm not allowed to post the picture any more, so I'll just keep asking the question.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Fair questions. I logged both nights as trespass and reported them to the harbourmaster. On the second night the person moved off up the slip toward the village when our floodlight swung across, which is what a person does. On the first night they didn't move at all, in two hails. I won't speculate past that. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding 3, apologies, it's a small one: the intermediary was dissolved about a month after the sale. That is common for single-purpose purchase vehicles and does not mean anything sinister. I mention it only because somebody will find it on their own and make it mean something.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Ewan, dear, you are not nosy, you are curious, which is different. 'They' is only what we say. My mother said it and her mother before. If you asked her who, she would say 'anyone who's out', and then she would put the kettle on, and that was the end of the matter. I have not got a better answer than hers.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: ha, anyway, my nan thinks they're putting a golf course on it... she's thought that about every empty bit of ground since the eighties, including the car park at the pier. I told her you can't play golf where the ball rolls into the sea. She said that's what the rich ones like.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Brackwater lights: still four minutes. A man in hi-vis behind the barrier was eating a pasty and looking into a hole, so I'm told that's the culvert works progressing. Gordon the cone has been moved to the other side of the road, where he looks lost.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Thank you all, and thank you Mrs Hale for letting 'you lot' pass. I'll stop counting windows from the ferry. Possibly. It was nice, this morning, to see them come on one after another as we came in, knowing what they were for, or at least what they are not for.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Sightlines. It's a mile of rock and weed with a strait on every side and a tide you'd not swim. Anybody coming can be seen now, trees or no trees. Folk are making a puzzle out of a woodcutting job. Grieve's boat goes over in the morning and comes back before dark, same as the curing boats did.

units.title: Pebble update, day 8
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Pebble update: still away. Tried the biscuit box last night and attracted two cats who are not Pebble and a fox who is very definitely not Pebble. Mr Arkle has lent me his ladder to look over the garage roofs behind Tanners Lane tomorrow. Grey, one white sock, green collar with a bell. Thank you, everyone.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: The public footpath is fine. The reservoir bank is not, and I have had people on the bank this week. As for stags, they do what they like at whatever hour they like. I have heard them clash at three in the morning in a hard frost. It's deer. Or it's somebody's idea of a joke with a mallet.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 20:00: 1019.6 hPa, wind southwest 3 and freshening, visibility 3 km and climbing. The fog signal stopped at 19:52. The silence afterwards is extraordinary; I could hear the kettle in the next room. Five days, eleven hours and nineteen minutes of fog by my station's count.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Heard it stop from the harbour. The whole quay went quiet and looked up, like somebody had switched off a radio in the next room. Out at five tomorrow. Aye, and glad of it.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Update from my house: I told the eldest at breakfast that it was a pasted sentence and a garage in Tollinby, and she was so disappointed she ate two breakfasts. The middle one is still holding out for a waterslide. The youngest wants to know if the trees mind. Thank you, planning lady.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: A fox at the biscuit box is a good sign, honestly: it means the sound carries. Keep going. And tell Mr Arkle to hold the ladder for you, not the other way round, we've had enough people falling off things in the fog this week.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: keeper bro chill, we're doing science out there. if its deer then the deer are insane. im bringing the thermal so we'll see the deer and the mallet guy. link in bio for the stream when it happens

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: deffo a lad. gilliver lads are famous for standing still in fog for fun lol. nothing else to do round here since they shut the arcade

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Dissolved a month after. Of course it was... Some companies only exist long enough to sign one piece of paper. I've said too much already. Watch what gets built, not what gets said.

units.title: spring tides this week
units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Spring tides from tomorrow, with low water around midday and midnight. The Gilliver slip will be exposed well below the usual weed line, and the bottom third is very slippery. Please take care, and please do not leave boats on trailers below the low-water mark. Byelaw 9. Thank you.

units.title: kettle update
units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Kettle update for the crew: new element, its own fused spur, no more trips. Tested it eleven times, made eleven teas, drank four. Also replaced a deck floodlight lamp on the starboard side that had gone dim, so it should swing a good deal brighter from tonight.

units.title: second report, Gilliver slip
units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: For the record and for the harbourmaster. Night of day 7, fog, 23:50 arrival at Gilliver. Someone on the slipway again, about two thirds of the way down, long dark coat. Smaller than the first night, by Kerris's eye and mine. When the deck floodlight swung across, they turned and walked up the slip toward the village. Hailed once, no answer. Logged it as trespass, reported it, carried on.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Confirming the skipper's log. Night 7 was a different one. This one moved, walked off like it had somewhere to be, and it was shorter. Night 4 didn't move, in two hails, and it was taller, too tall for a kid. I'm not saying anything more about night 4 than I've already said.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: night 7 one was defo a person, they slipped on the weed halfway up and windmilled their arms, I nearly laughed into the loudhailer, night 4 I was on the stern so I didn't see that one, kerris did, ok that's me being serious for once, don't get used to it

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you, skipper, I have both reports. Please could everyone remember that the slipway is not a place to stand at night, for very good reasons: it is steep, the weed is lethal at low water, and the ferry needs it clear. I will raise a sign with the parish council at its next meeting.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: seth if you want a fused spur for your own galley at home I've got the bits in the back. mates rates. lamps too

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: thats two nights then. right lads, nobody on the slip after dark, ive said it to my own nephews already. kerris finn thanks for being straight about it. anyone else wants to chat ghosts, sound board

units.title: breeze coming
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Glass is falling and there's a breath off the southwest. By the look of the gulls it'll clear tonight. Out at five tomorrow to see what's left of the pots. If anyone wants a hand lifting theirs I'll be on the Holm side by six, nowhere near their dock, before anybody asks.

units.title: Quay Road pole
units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Saw the Quay Road pole on the way past. Lorry took the stay wire out and the pole is leaning ten degrees toward the water. We'll have it changed this week. Twenty minutes off for two hundred houses is good going for a fog day. Don't park against flaming poles, anyone, they don't move but they do fall.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: I'm on the replacement crew. Garvey says I get to climb it. Garvey says that about every pole that's leaning. Question for him in public so he has to answer: why does the stay wire go on the opposite side to the lean, and not the same side?

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Because the stay holds it against the pull of the wires, Tess, not against gravity. Take the stay away and the conductors drag the pole over toward them. That's why it leans toward the sea, where the span is longest. You'll see when you're up it. Bring the good gloves.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: someone slipping on the weed in a long coat?? terrifying stuff lol. sounds like a tourist. or a heron like finn said
